entry_point.code: func (m *model) handleIntroductions(introducerCfg config.DeviceConfiguration, cm *protocol.ClusterConfig, folders map[string]config.FolderConfiguration, devices map[protocol.DeviceID]config.DeviceConfiguration)

trace.code: for _, folder := range cm.Folders { fcfg, ok := folders[folder.ID]; if !ok { continue }  // the folder ID comes straight from the remote introducer's ClusterConfig
if !fcfg.SharedWith(introducerCfg.DeviceID) { continue }  // the missing check in the vulnerable build: nothing verifies that this folder is shared with the introducer
for _, device := range folder.Devices { ... if fcfg.SharedWith(device.ID) { continue } ... }  // every device the introducer names, including the introducer itself, reaches the share-list append

fcfg.Devices = append(fcfg.Devices, config.FolderDeviceConfiguration{DeviceID: device.ID, IntroducedBy: introducerCfg.DeviceID}); folderChanged = true  // the introducer is now a member of a folder it was never given

handleIntroductions(...) return values are written back into the running configuration; the folder's Devices list is what the model uses to decide whether to serve index and file data to a connected device
if !fcfg.SharedWith(introducerCfg.DeviceID) { // The folder exists but is not shared with the introducer, so we don't trust them on the subject. continue }

preconditions: The victim has configured the attacker's device as an introducer (config.DeviceConfiguration.Introducer = true), e.g. a semi-trusted peer that is allowed to vouch for devices on folders it shares

The attacker knows the ID of another folder that exists on the victim but is not shared with the attacker (folder IDs are not secret; they are announced in ClusterConfig traffic and visible to connected devices)
The attacker can send a ClusterConfig message over its normal syncthing protocol connection and name itself (or any device) as a member of that folder

evidence.vulnerable_version: syncthing through v2.1.5 (bug present since the introducer feature was added; fixed in v2.1.6)
evidence.observed_result: Real syncthing lib/model source (vulnerable 466857a^ = v2.1.5) compiled with the Go toolchain. The driver calls model.handleIntroductions() with a real protocol.ClusterConfig in which the introducer announces a 'private' folder that is shared with another device but not with the introducer. Vulnerable build: the introducer is appended to private.Devices (SharedWith(introducer)=true, config changed=true) and syncthing logs 'Sharing folder vouched for by introducer'. Fixed build (upstream 466857ae applied): the same announcement is ignored for 'private' (SharedWith=false), while the legitimate introduction of a peer into the folder that IS shared with the introducer still succeeds.

real_exploit.target: syncthing/syncthing @ 2ca95cf1498104113fdfde46df4107f2450a0f71 (v2.1.5, real source tree) vs the same tree with upstream fix 466857ae applied
real_exploit.backend: real syncthing lib/model package compiled from the vendored upstream snapshot; model.handleIntroductions() is driven with real config.FolderConfiguration, config.DeviceConfiguration and protocol.ClusterConfig values
real_exploit.marker: RESULT: INTRODUCER FOLDER SCOPE ESCAPE CONFIRMED
real_exploit.demonstrated: An introducer can add itself to a folder that is not shared with it, escaping the documented introducer boundary (CWE-639/862 authorization bypass). The victim's config then lists the introducer as a folder member, which is the authorization input used to serve that folder's index and file data. The fixed build rejects the self-add while preserving legitimate introductions.
